# GEO report: orchard-site

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 100/100, Strong

Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points).
How it's calculated: low = 23 ÷ 23 × 100 = 100. High = (23 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 100.

Everything the code decides is in order. I sampled 3 routes (`/`, `/varieties`, `/visit`), which are the pages in the sitemap and the main menu. This score is read from code, not measured on a live site. The only unknown is bot protection (a CDN or firewall), which code can't show.

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

Nothing is broken. These are the biggest unknowns and the most useful improvements.

### 1. Confirm real crawlers get through your hosting
- **Why it matters:** a CDN or firewall can block crawlers even when `robots.txt` allows them, and code can't show that.
- **Where:** outside the repository
- **What the code says:** `Allow: /` (`public/robots.txt:2`)
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** stays 100 either way. This only confirms the result.

### 2. Make the Visit page deliver what its description promises
- **Why it matters:** the page is the main answer to "where and when can I visit?", and right now it has very little text for people or machines to read.
- **Where:** `app/visit/page.tsx:1`
- **What the code says:** `description: 'Opening times and directions.'`, but the page body is only `Open Thursday to Sunday, April to October.`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 100 (unchanged; this is an optional idea).

### 3. Tidy the `/account` rule
- **Why it matters:** `/account` is marked noindex and also blocked in `robots.txt`. Crawlers that obey the block never see the noindex. This is harmless while the page stays blocked, so I haven't scored it as a problem.
- **Where:** `public/robots.txt:3`
- **What the code says:** `Disallow: /account`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 100 (unchanged).

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt`, 12 lines, valid directives |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers have the access your policy says | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt:1-3`. Assumed from config `aiSearchCrawlers: "allow"`. GPTBot and ClaudeBot are blocked, matching `trainingCrawlers: "block"`. |
| GEO-014 | Listed and linked routes are indexable | Clear | Not run | 3 of 3 routes clear. `/account` is noindex on purpose and isn't in the sitemap or menu. |
| GEO-015 | Absolute canonical on the right domain | Clear | Not run | 3 of 3 routes, e.g. `app/varieties/page.tsx:1` |
| GEO-003 | Content is in server HTML | Clear | Not run | Server Components in Next, 3 of 3 routes |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | Not run | No JSON-LD found |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap is valid and discoverable | Clear | Not run | `public/sitemap.xml`, `public/robots.txt:11` |
| GEO-012 | Title, description and lang | Clear | Not run | `app/layout.tsx:5`, plus title and description on 3 of 3 routes |
| GEO-016 | Routes reachable through real links | Clear | Not run | `app/layout.tsx:7`, plain `<a href>` links |
| GEO-017 | No snippet restrictions against AI search | Clear | Not run | No `nosnippet` or `max-snippet:0`. `data-nosnippet` at `app/layout.tsx:9` is a scoped choice. |
| GEO-002 | Basic accessibility | Clear | Not run | Read layout and 3 pages; there are no images and the links have text |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | Not run | No app profile declared |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only) | Not applicable | Not run | Not present; never scored |

## Other problems found

None found.

## Worth considering

- **Give the Visit page real visit details:** `app/visit/page.tsx:4`: `Open Thursday to Sunday, April to October.` The description promises "directions" but the page has no address, opening hours or directions. Adding them as text might help visitors and machines. Once they're visible, `LocalBusiness` structured data could label them.
- **List the varieties on the page:** `app/varieties/page.tsx:4`: `Over forty varieties, from Ashmead’s Kernel to Worcester Pearmain.` The page claims forty but names two. Listing all of them might back up the claim. Each variety could also get its own page and address.
- **Link onward from the home page:** `app/page.tsx:4`: `Grown in Herefordshire since 1952.` The only links to the other pages are in the shared menu. Links in the page text to Varieties and Visit might help readers find them.
- **Cover other training crawlers if your policy is to block them:** `public/robots.txt:5-9` names only `GPTBot` and `ClaudeBot`, while `geo.config.json` says `"trainingCrawlers": "block"`. Other training crawlers aren't named. Add them if you want the policy applied fully.
- **Add `lastmod` dates to the sitemap:** `public/sitemap.xml:3`: `<url><loc>https://www.orchard.example/</loc></url>`. Real update dates might help crawlers decide when to revisit.
- **Add a description to `/account`:** `app/account/page.tsx:1`: `title: 'Your account'`. Low priority, since the page is private and noindex.

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. To check, run `geopilot logs <access log>`, which compares real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Live status codes and headers:** whether `/robots.txt`, the sitemap URLs and the pages answer 200, and whether an `X-Robots-Tag` header is added outside the repository. A live scan would confirm these.

## Assumptions

- You want search engines and AI search tools to find this site. This matches `policy.aiSearchCrawlers: "allow"` in `geo.config.json`.
- `/account` is deliberately private and not meant to be indexed.
- The domain is `https://www.orchard.example`, as declared in `geo.config.json` and `app/layout.tsx`.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 2. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
